problem_text:
A logistics firm must dispatch a specialized courier to four distinct regional warehouses, each positioned at precise coordinates on a grid representing the operational map.

Warehouse Alpha: Coordinates (3,23)
Warehouse Beta: Coordinates (184,102)
Warehouse Gamma: Coordinates (181,200)
Warehouse Delta: Coordinates (171,160)

The travel distances between pairs of warehouses, measured in kilometers, are predetermined:
Alpha to Gamma: 251.0 km
Alpha to Delta: 216.8 km
Beta to Gamma: 98.0 km
Beta to Delta: 59.4 km
Gamma to Delta: 41.2 km

Due to infrastructural limitations, no direct route exists connecting Warehouse Alpha and Warehouse Beta. Furthermore, the route plan must incorporate exactly one of two critical but mutually exclusive supply corridors: either the link between Beta and Gamma, or the link between Gamma and Delta.

The objective is to determine the most efficient closed-loop inspection circuit, wherein the courier visits each warehouse precisely once before returning to the origin, thereby minimizing the total travel distance.
